findings: AssetManager::tryLoadDdsOverride reads sidecar bytes directly on every call. Texture loads intentionally do not populate the raw file cache.

TerrainManager tile workers deduplicate M2/WMO preparation only inside PendingTile; workers for other tiles can read/analyze the same texture again. WMO normal-map generation is also performed before the GPU consumer cache lookup.
M2Renderer::loadTexture and WMORenderer::loadTexture check shared GPU cache later, after workers have prepared input. A GPU hit can avoid upload but cannot undo already completed worker I/O/analysis.

Character preparation reads RGBA separately from Stored world textures, and normal-map generation may reread source pixels. Different output forms are sometimes necessary; repeat count alone is not avoidable-work count.

File cache at 1 GiB limit with 36% aggregate hit rate suggests a candidate for instrumentation, not proof of cache thrashing. Misses include first reads and failed reads; DDS is not included in that miss counter.
GPU cache last sampled at 1.96 of 4 GiB and no full warning. No evidence that HD assets exhausted its configured capacity in this run.
All 25 measured DDS reads were previously seen paths, correcting the earlier description of these as new resources. New entities can reuse existing textures.
CPU texture reuse can reduce loading, allocations and frame tails; it does not by itself explain or remove the roughly 10.3ms M2 surface/RT GPU stage.
limits: Read counts are successful DDS override logs only, excluding BLP/PNG, failed attempts and unlogged paths.
Byte totals use current file sizes, not physical disk I/O; OS cache may serve reads.
